introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: A common explanation for the gap between AI capability and its use in managerial decisions is that AI and decision-making form two weakly connected communities separated by a Burt structural hole, where bridging gives information and control advantages. The premise motivated this project's own multi-level programming (MLP) model (idea.md sections 1-2).
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: The premise has been assumed, not tested with data that can carry Burt's construct. Much 'gap' evidence rests on co-occurrence or affiliation data, which cannot measure constraint or brokerage. Scope: the test covers (i) a literature corpus of 2,118 source documents coded into 10 x 12 function families (E1.1) and (ii) US utility patents granted 2010-2025 under CPC G06N vs G06Q10/04 + G06Q10/06, with applicant citations from citing years 2013-2025 (E3). Do not generalise beyond these data, these CPC operationalisations or US patents.

content_bullets: Unstructured, at most 200 words, no citations.
Premise: AI and decision-making are often described as communities separated by a structural hole. We test this rather than assume it (idea.md section 1).
Design: literature evidence (V5-V11.1) and four preregistered tests on 8,512,829 US utility patents (E3).

Domain result: AI and decision patents cite each other about three times the time-stratified expectation (OE 3.05, 95% CI 2.94-3.17). Both relative hole criteria fail; the verdict is HOLE_NOT_SUPPORTED in all 6 sensitivity checks (E3.1).
Firm result: specialist firms are separated, but a portfolio-preserving null reproduces 85-91% of that separation, and mixed-portfolio firms show no brokerage advantage (E3.4).
Literature result: depletions are directionally robust but do not survive realistic misclassification; no broker was confirmed (E1.5, E1.6).

Contributions: measurement lessons (co-occurrence is not flow; M06-P; portfolio-preserving null) and a multi-level programming agenda with a preregistered enterprise study. State that the organisational-bottleneck view is a hypothesis and that the model is simulated.

Motivation and premise (idea.md section 1): the 'two weakly connected communities' explanation and Burt's structural-hole framing. Present it as a widely used premise and the starting point of this project. Make no citation-free empirical claims about industry AI spending.
Say plainly that the project began with this premise and used it to motivate a multi-level programming model (idea.md section 1). The paper now tests the premise.
Measurement problem in one paragraph (idea.md section 2): Burt's construct needs real relations; constraint is mostly dyadic; co-occurrence is not flow. Preview Section 2.3.
Research questions RQ1, RQ2 and RQ3/RQ4 verbatim in substance from idea.md section 3.

What we do: Study 1 (literature, V5-V11.1; E1), Study 2 (US patents; four preregistrations frozen in public commits; E3), Study 3 (preregistered enterprise plan; idea.md section 8). Point to Figure fig_research_design.

Findings in brief, with numbers only from the log: OE(AI,DEC) = 3.05 (95% CI 2.94-3.17); H1a and H1b both FAIL; 0/6 sensitivity checks disagree (E3.1). Over-connection is PERSISTENT though declining (WLS slope -0.097 per year; E3.1 H2). No depleted CPC cell replicates across time halves (E3.3 P3). The specialist-firm O/E of 0.24 is 85% (primary) / 91% (S-tech) reproduced by the portfolio null, and MIXED firms show no brokerage advantage (E3.4). In Study 1, direction is defensible but significance is not, and there are 0 confirmed brokers (E1.5 verdict; E1.6).

Implication stated as a hypothesis (idea.md section 6 item 5; section 10): if firms struggle to integrate AI into decisions, the binding constraints more plausibly sit inside organisations. This is not a finding of Studies 1-2.

Contributions (idea.md section 9), each within the claim boundaries: (1) a preregistered negative result at the knowledge-flow level; (2) a measurement lesson listing four failure modes of co-occurrence data; (3) method contributions: M06-P and the portfolio-preserving firm null; (4) a reframing with a formal MLP model (simulated) and a preregistered calibration plan.
Roadmap of Sections 2-9.

Characterise these only at the level of their role notes in citation_map.json; do not attribute empirical results to them.

Define network constraint as Eq. (1), copied from idea.md section 2: c_i = sum over j in N(i) of (p_ij + sum over q != i,j of p_iq p_qj)^2, with p_ij the proportional tie strength. Explain the direct and indirect terms.
State the benefits claim (information and control) and that brokerage requires real ties and observed outcomes.
Measurement critiques: constraint mostly captures dyadic concentration; it is not an exclusive-brokerage index. Present this as reinterpretation, not refutation of the theory.
Measures are not interchangeable across network types. Betweenness alone does not establish Burt brokerage.
Brokerage roles need directed open two-paths with group membership (Gould-Fernandez; weighted version).

Study 2 uses examiner-assigned CPC labels: AI = G06N; DEC = G06Q10/04 (forecasting/optimisation) + G06Q10/06 (resources, workflow, management, decision analysis) (E3 data block).

Patent citations as records of prior art and a proxy for knowledge flows. Examiner-added citations are handled separately: the primary specification uses applicant citations, and s1 uses all categories (E3.1).

Ground the managerial premise in the verified AI-and-organisational-decision literature: decision structures with AI (shrestha2019organizational), the automation-augmentation paradox (raisch2021artificial), human-AI symbiosis (jarrahi2018artificial), managing AI in IS research (berente2021managing). Characterise these only at the level of their role notes in citation_map.json; do not attribute empirical results to them.
Co-occurrence data (functions appearing together in papers; organisations sharing projects) are two-mode affiliation data, not flows (idea.md section 2).

Formal point: in a strict bipartite graph the indirect term of constraint is identically zero (E1.6 Gap Validity V1; E3.3 P9). With equal tie weights, constraint therefore degenerates to 1/k (idea.md section 2). State the equal-weight condition explicitly.

Projections manufacture cliques. Illustrate with CORDIS H2020 (E2): the co-membership projection has 1,049 nodes and 12,181 edges and creates 102,660 within-project triads, while only 156 edges recur across >= 2 projects.

Two further failure modes from Study 1: same-term self-pairing (33% of records in the strongest enriched cell pair the same term; E1.3) and model-inferred labels with low human reliability (E1.4). These are previewed here and detailed in Section 4.
Conclusion: Burt's construct needs directed dyadic flows; patent citations provide them, and this motivates Study 2.

Corpus (E1.1): 2,118 source documents; 1,729 parsed; 26,501 candidate evidence records; 6,499 strict records. An LLM pipeline coded evidence sentences into 10 AI families x 12 decision families = 120 cells (idea.md section 4).

Frozen core rule: q <= .05 in main + exact + document-preserving tests with the same direction, plus raw. Result: 32 cells (16 enriched, 16 depleted).

subsections.subsection_title: 4.2 Direction and robustness of the depleted cells
content_bullets: Point to Appendix Table B1 for the 16 depleted cells and observed counts (E1.2). In the text give only the most extreme cell: PREDICTION_RISK_ESTIMATION x HUMAN_REVIEW_ACCOUNTABILITY, O = 6, E = 44.9.
Re-implementation (E1.3): exact and raw tests reproduce the official q values (|delta q| <= 6x10^-12); Jaccard overlap of the 32-cell core = .94.
20 Monte Carlo seeds: 31 cells are in the core under every seed, including all 16 depleted cells; 2 boundary cells are exactly the one-in / one-out pair of the human-corrected sidecar.
Track-stratified null: 16/16 depleted and 16/16 enriched cells remain significant with unchanged direction. Exclusion bias: depleted core cells pass the strict filter more often (38% vs 28%).
Two periods (<= 2023 vs >= 2024): 16/16 depleted in both; the change does not differ from a permutation null (p = .86). Present Figure fig_study1_direction.

Triangulation limits, stated plainly: keyword (stage-1) coding gives 13/16 same direction. Removing same-term self-pairs (33% in the strongest enriched cell) drops 2 prediction-related depleted cells from the core. The rule-based keyword matrix (741 same-term records removed, 1,431 document edges) gives 13/16 same direction, 6 significant, 0 significantly reversed, and only 7 cells reach the four-test core.
Summarise Study 1 robustness checks in Appendix Table B2 (E1.3).
TABLE 2 'Coding reliability' (source E1.4, all 7 rows, AI kappa and Decision kappa, exactly as logged). Kappa as defined by Cohen.

Key reading: human vs human agreement is very low (0.05 / 0.14). Two Claude models agree (0.72 / 0.56), but model-to-model agreement shows reproducibility, not human inter-rater reliability (E1.4; claim boundary vi).

Under codebook v2, 42-64% of evidence sentences state no explicit decision function, against a pipeline rate of 18%. Only about 9% of matrix records are reproduced in the same cell by both new coders (E1.4).

Analytic bound (E1.5) as Eq. (3): O_obs/E - 1 = (1 - e_AI)(1 - e_Dec)(T/E - 1). Random error can only attenuate a depletion; it cannot create one. For the most extreme cell, even the 95% upper bound needs an accuracy product >= 0.71, while the human audit implies about 0.07.

TABLE 3 'Misclassification simulation' (source E1.5, 6 scenarios; 300 runs each; median and 5th-95th percentile of still-significant and still-depleted cells). No scenario produced a spurious depleted cell.

Verdict as logged (E1.5, 2026-11-18): directional under-integration DEFENSIBLE; '16 statistically robust depleted pairs' NOT DEFENSIBLE as measured; Burt structural hole STOP; research gap NOT SUPPORTED.

Data (E3): USPTO PatentsView pvgpatdis, downloaded 2026-11-18; 8,512,829 utility patents granted 1976-2025; 152,631,929 citation rows; in scope (citing year 2010-2025) 87,414,291, of which 63,083,371 are applicant citations. Groups for grant years 2010-2025 (E3): AI 94,929; DEC 37,501; BRIDGE 5,316; other business-method patents (G06Q excluding G06Q10) 150,170. Bridge patents are excluded from the cross counts (idea.md section 5.1).

Eq. (4) time-stratified configuration expectation: E(A->B) = sum over s of out_A(s) in_B(s) / M(s), s = (citing grant year, cited grant year). Eq. (5) symmetric intensity: OE(A,B) = [O(A->B) + O(B->A)] / [E(A->B) + E(B->A)].
Hypotheses H1a and H1b as preregistered (idea.md section 5.1; E3.1). H1a reference set: 179 CPC main groups in G06/G16/H04 with >= 2,000 patents.

Primary result (E3.1): O = 30,843, E = 10,112, OE(AI,DEC) = 3.05 (95% CI 2.94-3.17; Poisson cluster bootstrap over citing patents, 2,000 reps). AI->DEC O/E 3.26 (O 21,820, E 6,686); DEC->AI O/E 2.63 (O 9,023, E 3,426).

H1a: OE exceeds 97.8% of OE(AI,X) and 92.2% of OE(DEC,X). Reference lowest-quartile values are 0.787 (AI) and 0.502 (DEC); medians 1.240 and 1.095. FAIL. H1b: ratio 1.69 (95% CI 1.60-1.77), with OE(AI,BIZ-OTHER) = 1.809. FAIL.

TABLE 5 'Aggregate test: primary and preregistered sensitivity specifications' (source: E3.1 sensitivity table, 7 rows: OE, ratio vs BIZ with CI, percentiles AI/DEC, verdict). Present Figure fig_patent_sensitivity. Verdict HOLE_NOT_SUPPORTED; 0/6 sensitivity checks disagree; not fragile.

H2 trend (E3.1): present Figure fig_patent_trend. WLS slope -0.097 per year (95% CI -0.130 to -0.065); last-3-year OE 2.69 against a reference median of 1.095; preregistered label PERSISTENT. Full yearly table in Appendix Table B3.
Answer RQ1 at the domain level: AI and decision technologies are over-connected, not separated. Word it as 'not supported', not as proof of absence.

subsections.subsection_title: 5.2 The V9 battery on the CPC matrix and the M06-P null
content_bullets: Matrix (E3.2): 6 AI-method rows (G06N3, G06N5, G06N7, G06N10, G06N20, G06N_OTHER) x 7 decision-function columns (FORECAST_OPTIMISE G06Q10/04; RESOURCE_SCHEDULING /0631; WORKFLOW /0633; RISK /0635; STRATEGY /0637; PERFORMANCE /0639; MGMT_GENERAL other /06) = 42 cells. The engine is a byte-identical copy of the V9 engine (SHA-256 09c3d60c...bc33).

Parts (E3.2): A co-classification, 5,316 patents and 14,573 edges. B applicant citations between AI-only and DEC-only patents, 30,843 citations and 66,056 edges. B all categories: 38,252 citations and 80,849 edges.

Methodological finding: the original M06 document-preserving swap accepted 0 of 21,843,600 swaps. Each document contributes a complete row x column block, so every swap targets an existing edge. The preregistered core is 0 by construction and uninformative (amendment B1).
Define M06-P: permute column sets among documents within (|rows|, |cols|) strata. Both margins and the block structure are preserved; 5,000 samples (E3.2; idea.md section 5.2).
Results (E3.2): adapted full core A 8 depleted / 7 enriched; B 9 / 8; B all categories 8 / 8. q <= .05 cells by test (main / exact / raw / M06-P): A 20 / 20 / 29 / 22; B 22 / 22 / 27 / 25.

TABLE 6 'Cells depleted in both co-classification (A) and citation flow (B)' (source: E3.2 table, 5 rows with O/E and observed/expected). Note that the quantum row is tiny (74 edges in A). List the 4 cells enriched in both in the text (E3.2).

Present Figure fig_cpc_heatmap. Emphasise magnitude: apart from the quantum cell, depleted O/E values lie between 0.70 and 0.95 (Table 6). These are small deviations inside an over-connected pair; they are not separations and never 'gaps' (claim boundary ii).
Explain that every original Study 1 line has a patent analogue (idea.md section 5.3), and present P2-P10 in that order.

P2 V9.1 calibration (E3.3): seeds (20 x 10,000): A has 20 cells always q <= .05 and 4 boundary cells; B has 22 always and 0 boundary. 1,000 stub-permutation null matrices: mean false cells per matrix 0.045 (A) / 0.049 (B); share of matrices with any false cell 3.6% / 4.4%. Power for a 20% depletion in cells with E >= 100: 18/27 = 67% (A), 23/29 = 79% (B). Segmentation S1/S2 counts and overlaps as logged.
P3 time split (E3.3): A 2010-2017 0 depleted vs 2018-2025 8; B 2013-2018 3 vs 2019-2025 11. 0 depleted cells replicate in both halves, in A or B. Cell-level depletions are time-unstable.

P4 label face validity: all 11 labels pass the lift >= 1.5 criterion (full lifts in Appendix Table B5). This replaces the human audit of Study 1; say that it is a title-keyword check, not a human coding audit.

P5 firm network (E3.3): 6,201 organisations with ties; 20,681 ties (total weight 109,508 applicant citations; self-citations excluded). Groups: 2,926 AI_FIRM, 1,570 DEC_FIRM, 1,705 MIXED. Group O/E: AI_FIRM~DEC_FIRM 0.24 (O 886, E 3,700); AI_FIRM~MIXED 0.81; DEC_FIRM~MIXED 0.97. The preregistered firm-level hole criterion is met at this stage. Median Burt constraint: AI_FIRM 0.62, DEC_FIRM 0.76, MIXED 0.36. Against a degree-matched label-permutation null: null median 0.444, one-sided p = .001.
Make clear that the P5 criterion being met motivated preregistration 4 (Section 5.4) and is not a confirmed structural hole (claim boundary i).

P6 removal falsification: after removing the 10 lowest-constraint MIXED candidates (degree >= 5), AI_FIRM and DEC_FIRM firms remain connected. The largest component containing both groups falls from 5,954 to 5,563 firms. 10/10 candidates are refuted as indispensable brokers. The cross-weight-retained metric is identically 1 by construction and therefore uninformative. If candidate firms are named (E3.3 P5 list), name them only as refuted candidates.
P7: 2,546 co-assignment hyperedges; 32% join an AI_FIRM with a DEC_FIRM or MIXED firm. P8: 54 firms checked; 0 possible alias collisions.

P9 Gap Validity: the indirect constraint term is 0 (bipartite); every depleted cell has 20-30 alternative length-3 routes; depleted cells at q <= .01 vs q <= .05: A 7 vs 9, B 9 vs 10. P10 Limitation Scout: NOT_APPLICABLE.
Summary table of P2/P3/P9 in Appendix Table B4.
Rationale (idea.md section 5.4): the firm-level pattern could be mechanical. Mixed-portfolio firms own both kinds of patents, and patents cite within their field.

Null (E3.4): permute patents' owner sets within strata. This keeps every firm's portfolio and group and the whole patent-level citation network fixed. Primary strata: patent type x grant year (48 strata). S-tech strata: type x year x AI rows x DEC columns (1,795 strata). 1,000 replicates each; replicate r uses seed sequence [20261119, s, r]. Scope: 127,114 patents, 14,600 firms, 162,339 citations. The identity permutation reproduces P5 exactly.
TABLE 7 'Portfolio-preserving firm null' (source: E3.4 table, 4 statistics x observed / primary null median [95%] / p / S-tech null median [95%] / p).
Present Figure fig_firm_null. Share of the T1 gap reproduced by the null: 85% (primary), 91% (S-tech).

Interpretation (E3.4): the verdict is PARTIAL in both stratifications, so it is not sensitive to technology mix. Specialist separation is mostly a portfolio effect. The lower constraint of MIXED firms does not survive: observed 0.358 vs null medians 0.104 / 0.116, p = 1.000, so real firms are more clustered than the null and mixed firms show no brokerage advantage.

Contrast with P5: against a degree-matched label null, MIXED constraint looked low (p = .001). Against a portfolio-preserving null it does not. The choice of null determines the brokerage conclusion, which sets up the measurement lesson in Section 6.2.
Answer RQ2: no firm-level structural hole beyond what portfolios mechanically imply. A residual specialist separation remains unexplained by the null; report it without interpretation as a hole.

subsections.subsection_title: 6.1 What the three data lines jointly show
content_bullets: Restate idea.md section 6 items 1-4 with evidence pointers: (1) the domain level is over-connected and persistently so, though declining (E3.1); (2) cell-level depletions are small and time-unstable (E3.2 Table 6; E3.3 P3); (3) specialist firms are separated, but 85-91% of that is a portfolio effect, and mixed firms have no brokerage advantage (E3.4); (4) no line confirms a Burt structural hole (E1.6; E2; E3.3-E3.4).

Define the 'three data lines' explicitly when first used. Proposed: (i) literature co-occurrence and network lines (Study 1, E1); (ii) public organisational sources (E2, CORDIS bipartite null: 0 significant); (iii) US patent citations at domain, cell and firm level (Study 2, E3). Add that only (iii) is flow-valid. idea.md does not define the three lines; see the inconsistency list.

Reconcile the apparent tension. Study 1 finds persistent cell-level depletion within the AI-decision literature (E1.3, p = .86 for period change), while patents show domain-level over-connection (E3.1). These are different units and references: function co-occurrence relative to matrix margins vs domain-to-domain citation relative to all fields. Cell-level depletions in both data lines are relative deviations, not separation.

Answer RQ1 and RQ2 together, in negative and claim-bounded terms: the evidence does not support a structural hole between AI and decision knowledge domains or between firms, beyond portfolio composition. Do not claim causal effects (claim boundary iii).

Four failure modes of co-occurrence/affiliation data (idea.md section 9 item 2), each with its evidence: projection cliques (E2 CORDIS: 102,660 triads vs 156 recurring edges); bipartite degeneration of constraint (E1.6 Gap Validity; E3.3 P9); same-term self-pairing (E1.3, 33%); model-inferred labels with low human reliability (E1.4).

Null-model lessons (idea.md section 9 item 3): the document-preserving swap is degenerate on block-structured documents (0 of 21,843,600 swaps accepted; E3.2), and M06-P preserves both margins and block structure. The portfolio-preserving null separates firm brokerage from portfolio composition (E3.4). A degree-matched label null gave the opposite reading (E3.3 P5).

Design lessons: test relative rather than absolute OE because citing is field-local (idea.md section 5.1); calibrate on synthetic data before real data (E3.1 synthetic calibration); report preregistered stop rules and amendments (Section 3.3).
Practical guidance for researchers who study 'gaps' between AI and decision functions: a depleted cell is not a gap, and a low-constraint node is not a broker without a portfolio-aware null.

subsections.subsection_title: 6.3 Where the integration problem may sit: a hypothesis
content_bullets: idea.md section 6 item 5: the AI-decision integration problem is not a knowledge-flow gap. If firms struggle to integrate AI into decisions, the binding constraints more plausibly sit inside organisations: resource allocation, decision rights and governance, and human-AI configuration.
State twice and plainly that this is a hypothesis, not a finding of Studies 1-2 (claim boundary v), and that the studies contain no organisation-internal data.
Link to embeddedness: integration happens in concrete organisational relations, which is the level the MLP model represents and Study 3 will observe.
Transition to Section 7.

Set-up (idea.md section 7): processes i in I; capability resources r in {D (data), A (AI), R (reliability), G (governance)}; governance regime Gamma; budget B_tot. Position the model in bilevel and multilevel programming.

Level 1 (leader), Eq. (6): b_i^r in {0,1,2,3}; sum over i,r of c_i^r b_i^r <= B_tot; capabilities X-bar_i = phi_X(X_i^0, b_i^X) with toy map phi_X = min(3, X^0 + b); F1 = 1.25 RealizedValue + 0.20 AIAdoptions - 0.22 ResourceUse - 0.75 ResidualRisk.

Level 2, Eq. (7): (A_i, H_i, WI_i, EA_i) in {0..3}^4 with capability ceilings and the shared capacity constraint sum over i of (0.42A + 0.24H + 0.24EA + 0.20WI) <= K_Gamma. F2 aggregates feasibility, reliability, scalability, integration cost, governance risk and Level-3 utility. Requirement thresholds go to Appendix C.

Level 3, Eq. (8): q_im in {0,1}, sum over m of q_im = 1 over the five configurations (HumanOnly, AIAssist, HumanFirstAICheck, AIFirstReview, BoundedAutomation); q_im <= Allow_m,Gamma; U_im = Gain - 0.45 Burden - 0.75 ResidualRisk.

Properties: under the stated assumptions (finite domains; zero allocation feasible; HumanOnly always feasible; separable followers; deterministic tie-breaking) a selected tri-level profile exists and exhaustive backward induction terminates. This is not a tractability claim. If followers share constraints, a coupled or generalised equilibrium concept is needed; Nash is only a boundary reference.

Say that the original v1.0 governing source was the 16 V9 depleted cells. This paper does not use them as validated empirical gaps; the thresholds are design assumptions to be calibrated in Study 3 (idea.md section 7).
Open with the boundary: all coefficients are simulated; there is no internal company data; outputs describe no real firm (E4; claim boundary iv).

Exactness checks (E4): exact backward induction over 3 processes, governance regimes C/F/D and budgets 3/5/7. Generator vs canonical domain check: 768 cases, 3,121 canonical-feasible state occurrences, 0 mismatches. Mutation sensitivity 720/768 detected. Runtime 13.9 s.

Regimes are parameter sets only; do not expand C/F/D. Parameters (K, risk, cost and flexibility multipliers) are in Appendix Table C1. In the baseline all five configurations are permitted under every regime.
TABLE 8 'Simulated baseline scenarios' (source: E4 nine-scenario table; columns governance, budget, F1, realised value, residual risk, AI adoptions, configurations). Present Figure fig_mlp_scenarios.
Describe the pattern without causal language: under C and F, budget 7 gives the same solution as budget 5. Under D at budget 7 one process moves to HumanFirstAICheck (F1 2.616).

Governance permission probe (E4; C, B = 5): restricting configuration permissions lowers F1 from 2.158 to 0.837, and configurations change from AIAssist x3 to HumanOnly x2 + HumanFirstAICheck x1. Use this only to show the mechanism the model represents (permission-bound rather than capability-bound), not as evidence.

Selection-threshold sensitivity (E4; process P2, score 0.65, truth 1): at tau <= 0.6, P2 uses AIAssist (F1 2.244); at tau = 0.7, Level 1 allocates nothing to P2's AI capability and P2 reverts to HumanOnly (F1 1.450). The writer must define tau in one sentence consistent with E4 only; idea.md does not define it (see the inconsistency list).

subsections.subsection_title: 7.3 Study 3: a preregistered enterprise study (plan, not results)
content_bullets: Aim (idea.md section 8): locate where AI-decision integration breaks inside organisations, and calibrate the MLP parameters.
Unit and sample: decision processes within one or more manufacturing firms. The firm is identified in the thesis and anonymised in this paper.

TABLE 9 'Study 3 data mapped to model levels' (source: idea.md section 8 table: Level 1 budgets and staffing; Level 2 approval/audit workflows and decision-rights matrices; Level 3 process observation and interviews; optional organisational structural-hole test on de-identified ticket and meeting metadata with Burt constraint and the portfolio-style nulls of Study 2).

Preregistered decision rules, to be frozen before data access: what supports an organisational bottleneck (feasible configurations blocked by Allow_m,Gamma or K_Gamma rather than by capability ceilings); what contradicts it (capability ceilings or data quality bind first); a stop rule.
The three-expert translation exercise is a pilot for the instruments, not evidence (idea.md section 8).
Say that Study 3 tests the hypothesis of Section 6.3; no result is reported or implied.
Mandatory and explicit section; it overrides any instruction to avoid stating limitations.

Study 1 coding reliability is low (human kappa 0.05 / 0.14; E1.4), and significance does not survive realistic misclassification (E1.5). The 16 depleted cells are not '16 statistically robust depleted pairs' (E1.5 verdict). Model-to-model agreement (0.72 / 0.56) is not human reliability.
V6-V11.1 network results are HISTORICAL / USER_REPORTED; their raw files were not re-verified (E1.6).

CPC classes are proxies for knowledge domains. 'Decision' is operationalised as G06Q10/04 + G06Q10/06 (s2 broadens it to all G06Q10; E3.1). Label validity rests on a title-keyword lift check (P4), not a human audit.

Patent citations are an imperfect flow proxy. Examiner citations are excluded from the primary specification only through PatentsView categories; applicant-only analysis effectively starts in 2013 (E3). The data cover US patents only and patented inventions, not organisational practice.
Firm identities rely on disambiguated assignees; the alias check covered 54 firms (E3.3 P8). No external source passed the flow-validity gates, and SEC data were not fetched (E2).
All results are associational; no causal effects are claimed (claim boundary iii).

A failure to support a hole is not proof that no hole exists in other data, other operationalisations or other countries. Synthetic calibration detected 30% and 50% suppression (E3.1). Cell-level power for a 20% depletion with E >= 100 was 67% (A) and 79% (B) (E3.3 P2), so smaller cells or weaker depletions may be missed.
M06-P was introduced by amendment B1 after the preregistered M06 proved degenerate (E3.2); it is a documented deviation, not part of the original frozen plan.

The portfolio null reproduces 85% (primary) / 91% (S-tech) of the specialist separation (E3.4), so the rest is unexplained. Do not state a derived residual percentage, which is not in the log. Report the residual as unexplained, not as a hole. The P6 cross-weight-retained metric is uninformative by construction (E3.3).
Cell-level patent depletions do not replicate across time halves (E3.3 P3), and the quantum row is tiny (74 edges in A; E3.2).

subsections.subsection_title: 8.3 The model and the organisational hypothesis
content_bullets: All MLP coefficients are simulated and uncalibrated; outputs reflect no real firm (E4; claim boundary iv).
Exact enumeration of a bounded 3-process prototype is not evidence of tractability at scale (Jeroslow). Shared follower constraints would need a generalised equilibrium concept (idea.md section 7).

'The bottleneck is organisational' is a hypothesis for Study 3, not a result (claim boundary v). Study 3 is a plan in one or more manufacturing firms, which will limit generalisation; the expert translation exercise is a pilot only (idea.md section 8).
Answer RQ1: knowledge-domain evidence does not support a structural hole; AI and decision patents are over-connected (OE 3.05; HOLE_NOT_SUPPORTED; E3.1).
Answer RQ2: firm-level separation is mostly a portfolio effect (85-91%), and mixed firms are not brokers (E3.4).
Restate the measurement lesson in one sentence: co-occurrence is not flow, and the null model must preserve the structure that generates the data.
RQ3/RQ4: the integration question moves to the organisation as a hypothesis, with a formal (simulated) MLP model and a preregistered Study 3 to calibrate it. End without promotional language.
Generated from citation_map.json only (26 keys) with natbib author-year and an APA-like style (apalike). Every one of the 26 keys is cited at least once in the plan above. No other references.
